title: When Beijing Floods, the 600-Year-Old Forbidden City Drains Itself | China Travel Expert
description:
When modern Beijing flooded in July 2016, the 600-year-old Forbidden City stayed dry and drained itself. How does Ming-era plumbing beat a modern city's pipes?

The Palace Museum sits on ground that slopes from the higher north to the lower south, so rain runs off on its own. Carved stone dragon heads (螭首 chīshǒu) line the marble terraces and "spit" the rain clear of the halls. From there it drops into open ditches and then a network of channels — more than 15 km of them, with around 13 km running underground — that empties into the Inner Golden Water River and out to the palace moat. In the July 2016 storms that flooded parts of modern Beijing, the system kept the Forbidden City's halls dry.

🧭 Expert Tip: come on a rainy day — that is when you can actually watch the dragon-head spouts throw water off the terraces.

北京暴雨内涝，600年的紫禁城却能自己排水——靠的是北高南低的坡度、螭首排水口和十几公里的暗沟。
